absent: Full field layout and size of connection, buffer, reply, status and feature structures beyond the individual members observed in these fragments.
Initial values, allocation points and teardown order for global locks, connection pointer, queues, wait objects and control state.
Detailed backlog, rate limit, loss accounting and failure mode behavior outside the observed queue and counter operations.
Complete netlink protocol, group identifiers, message type values and userspace compatibility expectations beyond the observed send and receive paths.
Remaining branches of the central message dispatcher after the truncated user message section and any unobserved configuration cases.
Lifetime, locking and reference rules for buffers, sockets and namespaces beyond the observed acquire and release pairs.
Exact security context, credential and namespace translation semantics beyond the observed logging and admission checks.

findings.text: Global audit formatting helpers provide task identity, path, terminal and untrusted string services to other kernel parts. The set covers task information, executable path, generic path, terminal reference handling and several string encodings with control detection. Callers supply a log buffer plus source data and receive formatted output or a boolean control verdict.

Global reply helpers build a netlink reply message from sequence, type and payload and drive asynchronous list transmission. One allocates and populates a message buffer, returning absence on allocation failure. The other transmits a queued list to a recorded destination then releases network and list resources.

Background log pump runs as a freezable kernel thread until stopped. It repeatedly snapshots the current daemon connection, flushes pending queues, wakes backlog waiters, then sleeps until the main queue holds work. Multicast delivery continues even without a connected daemon.

Asynchronous responders run as short lived kernel threads plus a central message dispatcher. List and single reply threads first serialize against control handling, then unicast already built messages and release their context. The dispatcher validates and routes status, feature and user message requests.

Daemon reset only clears when the supplied handle matches the current connection or when no handle is supplied, otherwise it leaves state untouched. On clear it nulls the global pointer under lock, defers old connection reclamation, and moves every retry entry to hold with a refused indication while leaving the main queue for normal multicast processing.

Unicast to the daemon never transmits while holding read protection. It snapshots network reference, socket and port identifier under protection, releases protection, then transmits. Missing connection frees the message and reports refusal. A refused transmit triggers a reset of the snapshot connection.

Queue transmission processes only entries present at entry by remembering the tail, invoking an optional per message hook, and diverting to an error hook when no destination exists. Failures retry up to a supplied limit, with refusal and permission treated as fatal and causing destination abandonment plus continued draining. Success clears the consecutive failure count.

Multicast delivery is best effort to the read log group using the initial network context. It does nothing without listeners and drops silently on copy allocation failure. It transmits a copy rather than sharing the original buffer and aligns the header length with the source length before sending.

Netlink admission restricts configuration and user message families separately. Non initial user context is reported as refused to preserve login behavior. Rule management requests are unsupported. Configuration family requires initial process identity context and control privilege. User message family requires write privilege. Unknown types are invalid.

Feature state consists of enable bits plus sticky lock bits with a two phase update. Validation scans masked features and rejects any change to an already locked bit while logging denial. Application then logs each actual change, sets or clears enable bits, and accumulates new locks. Locks never clear.

Untrusted text encoding branches on control presence. A string counts as controlled if it contains quotation or any byte outside the printable range. Controlled content uses hexadecimal form, otherwise quoted literal form. Length limited and null terminated variants delegate to the bounded forms.

Log buffer appends tolerate absent buffers by doing nothing and grow on demand with overflow safety. Hexadecimal form needs twice the source length, quoted form needs the source plus enclosing marks. Arithmetic overflow or failed growth results in a placeholder mark rather than corruption, and successful growth appends without including the terminator in length.

Task identity logging records parent and thread group identifiers, login user, real and group credentials, extended credential set, terminal name or a none marker, session, command name as untrusted text, executable path and security context. Missing log buffer results in no action.

Path logging prefixes output then renders the filesystem path as untrusted text with bounded temporary storage allowing room for a deletion suffix. Allocation failure and overlong rendering each produce distinct quoted markers instead of failing. Executable lookup through memory management falls back to a null marker when unavailable.

Daemon pointer is protected by a spin lock with interrupt state saved for mutation and by read protection for observation. Mutation dereferences under lock, checks identity, nulls with ordered store, unlocks, then defers reclamation. Observation copies needed fields under read protection and drops protection before any potentially blocking transmit.

Current task terminal reference is acquired under the sighand signal lock with interrupt state saved, only if signal state exists, using reference counted acquisition. Release drops the reference without additional locking and tolerates absence.

Control serialization and queue ownership separate concerns. Reply threads briefly acquire then release the control lock to wait for the parent control operation to finish before transmitting. Queue draining assumes the background thread already holds required exclusion and relies solely on passed socket and port information.

Reply context carries a message buffer, a network reference and a destination port identifier, with cleanup releasing buffer, network reference and container while tolerating absent parts. Built replies encode sequence, resolved type that prefers completion indication over supplied type when done, multipart flag, and a copied payload of stated size.

Three socket buffer queues separate lifecycle stages. Main holds fresh records awaiting first multicast plus unicast attempt. Retry holds records whose unicast failed but daemon remains plausible. Hold holds records accumulated while no daemon can receive, fed from retry on reset and from main when destination is absent.

Background thread cycles through ordered phases each iteration with snapshot, hold flush with rehold on error, retry flush with hold on error using a fixed retry budget, then main processing with multicast per message and retry or hold on error depending on destination availability. Any negative flush aborts later unicast, resets the daemon, releases network reference, wakes waiters and sleeps until main holds work.

Daemon identity registration enforces a single healthy owner. Setting a non zero identifier must match the requester, probes the new connection, rejects replacement of a live daemon as exists, and rejects unregister by non owner as access denied. New registration records port and network, logs success, and wakes the pump. Zero clears the connection and logs.

Message handling branches after admission. Status queries reply with current counters and limits. Status updates apply masked fields with range checks and atomic counter exchanges for loss statistics. Feature queries reply with current set, feature updates require a full structure. User messages are dropped when disabled except for a specific access control type, require minimal length, pass a filter, handle terminal push for terminal type, then log with sender identity.

Transmitting while holding read protection or without holding a network reference risks use after free. The design avoids this by limiting protected regions to pointer dereference and field copying, acquiring a network reference inside the region, and performing all blocking sends and resets after release.

Sharing the original buffer for multicast would expose non standard modifications expected by legacy unicast consumers, so a copy is mandatory. Treating temporary resource shortage as fatal would discard queues, so that specific failure is normalized to success after draining. Length arithmetic uses checked operations to avoid wrap, falling back to a marker.

Unicast retry budget for background flushing of hold and retry queues is 5 attempts per queue per iteration, while main queue uses a single attempt. This bound limits transient failure retries before abandoning the destination for that iteration.
